initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the file can show annual counts of pedestrian injuries and deaths in Brooklyn crashes, but it has no pedestrian exposure measure (such as trips, walking distance, or population) to establish risk per pedestrian or whether safety per unit of exposure improved
initial_plan.metric: annual number of pedestrians injured or killed, calculated as the sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured and number_of_pedestrians_killed
initial_plan.denominator: none; an annual count of pedestrian casualties
initial_plan.population: pedestrians injured or killed in police-reported crashes whose borough is Brooklyn
filters: exclude incomplete calendar year(s) after the data check
exclude rows missing either pedestrian outcome count
initial_plan.years: calendar years from 2013 through the latest complete year represented in the file; identify completeness from the data check

data_check.facts: The complete years in scope are 2013–2025, with date coverage from January 1 through December 31 in each. The candidate 2026 year is partial (January 1–June 11) and has 9,700 Brooklyn crash rows. There are 473,801 Brooklyn crash rows across the selected complete years; missing/default borough rows and missing crash dates within the selected population are each 0. Missing number_of_pedestrians_injured rows and missing number_of_pedestrians_killed rows are each 0. There are no unrepresented calendar years between 2013 and 2026.
data_check.decisions: Exclude the 9,700 rows dated in partial 2026 rather than compare a partial year with full years. Keep the complete-year rows; no rows are dropped for missing pedestrian outcome counts. The borough and crash-date filters leave no missing/default group values in the selected population.
data_check.plan_change: Set the latest included year to 2025 based on observed full-year date coverage; all other initial definitions remain.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: the measure describes recorded pedestrian casualties in Brooklyn crashes, but without pedestrian exposure (such as walking trips, distance, or population) it cannot establish whether risk per pedestrian improved
final_plan.metric: annual pedestrian casualties: sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed
final_plan.denominator: none; annual count of pedestrian casualties
final_plan.population: pedestrians injured or killed in police-reported crashes with borough normalized to Brooklyn
filters: borough normalized by trim and uppercase = BROOKLYN
exclude rows missing either summed pedestrian outcome count
final_plan.years: complete calendar years 2013–2025 inclusive; exclude partial 2026 (January 1–June 11)
final_plan.limitations: This is an annual count, not a pedestrian risk rate: the dataset has no walking exposure denominator. Brooklyn crash-row totals in the check file by year (2013–2025) are 47,024; 47,761; 50,851; 47,464; 44,915; 47,313; 44,479; 25,473; 25,174; 23,369; 22,890; 22,785; and 24,303, so changes in recorded casualty counts are not adjusted for changes in the number of crash rows. All 473,801 selected rows have both summed outcome fields present; the 9,700 rows in partial 2026 are excluded.
